absent: Locking discipline for fixed mapping installation and page table allocation is not shown in these fragments.
Signal handling and scheduler interaction behind user return notifiers and deferred FPU switching are not shown.
Complete fixed slot ordering values and address top selection conditions beyond the two variants are not shown.
Floppy controller register semantics and native DMA controller programming details are not shown.
Machine check recovery beyond spinning and full exception handler dispatch beyond BPF decline are not shown.

findings.text: The architecture defines two hypervisor emulation trap prefixes, one for Xen and one for KVM, each combining an invalid opcode pair with three identifier bytes spelling the hypervisor name.
Enclave leaf selectors for the unprivileged enclave instruction use small integer identifiers, with enter assigned two, resume assigned three, and exit assigned four.

Exception table fixup data packs four fields in one word with low byte for handler type, next nibble for register selector, next nibble for flag selector, and upper half for immediate value, with shifts of eight twelve and sixteen and helpers placing each field.
Segment related register selectors use register field values eight through eleven for DS ES FS GS, and flag selectors use flag values one through three to request clearing of AX, DX, or both.

Lower fault handler type numbers assign zero to none, one to default, two to fault, three to user access, five to clear FS, six to FPU restore, seven to BPF, eight to WRMSR, nine to RDMSR, ten and eleven to safe MSR variants reporting IO error, twelve and thirteen to MSR inside machine check, fourteen and fifteen to machine check safe default and fault.

Higher handler types assign sixteen to pop register with stack growth, seventeen to immediate to register with derived fault zero and one variants, eighteen to SGX fault, nineteen to user copy length scaled by immediate with one four and eight variants, twenty to zeropad load, and twenty one to ERETU.

Fixed mapping area uses two directory entries in one build and a computed count in another, top index five hundred seven, sixty four boot maps times eight slots for temporary mappings, and derived start and size values from top minus permanent and total counts scaled by page size.

Exception table entries hold three relative integer fields describing the faulting instruction location, the fixup location, and associated handler data, with architecture support for relative tables and a helper exchanging fixup and data between two entries adjusted by a delta.

Fixed addresses form an enumeration of reserved slots for debug, early console, local and IO APICs, temporary kernel maps, paravirt bootmap, GHES, and aligned temporary boot maps, terminated by permanent and total end markers from which virtual start addresses derive.

Entry from user mode in debug builds validates that native saved flags have direction and nested task bits clear plus alignment bit clear when SMAP or Xen paravirt is present, that register state indicates user mode and matches current task registers, and that execution is on the normal thread stack, warning once on violation.

Thread stack membership is determined by comparing the current stack pointer against a per CPU top of stack value, sourced from a constant or stable per CPU variable depending on segment support configuration.

Exit to user mode preparation asserts floating point state consistency, services pending thread work, refreshes the FRED shadow stack pointer, clears compat tracking after signal handling where applicable, and issues an indirect branch barrier once when flagged, while final exit clears the AMD divider.
Pending exit work dispatches three optional actions based on thread flags, covering user return notification, IO bitmap refresh, and deferred FPU loading.

FRED return stack update recomputes the thread stack top and writes the dedicated control register only when the feature is enabled and the cached per CPU value differs, while the non serializing register write uses an alternative instruction sequence protected by a WRMSR exception table entry.

Establishing a fixed mapping sanitizes protection bits against the default kernel mask, converts physical address to page frame, rejects indices beyond the enumeration end, installs the entry through the kernel page table walk, and accounts the operation, with late aliases reusing the same primitive for set and clear.

Sixty four bit fixed mapping installation walks down from the kernel top level through intermediate levels, allocating missing tables from zeroed pages before or after boot memory, populating each level with table permissions, setting the leaf entry, and flushing the single kernel mapping.

Thirty two bit fixed mapping installation requires all intermediate levels to already exist and clears or sets the leaf depending on emptiness, while allocation hooks and IO bitmap update and divider clear and FPU assert and ESP fix init each have empty versus paravirt or feature gated variants.

Floppy port reads and writes add multiple IO delay intervals after each access, interrupt and DMA control wrappers select native or virtual handlers, residue accounting combines remaining count with accumulated residue, and DMA crossing of a sixty four kilobyte boundary is detected only for non virtual transfers.

Public fixed mapping and page table helpers expose setting a fixed entry, native fixed entry installation, walking and installing a kernel virtual entry on both sixty four and thirty two bit builds, and populating upper directory levels with TLB maintenance.

User mode transition hooks cover entry from user mode, pending work service during exit preparation, final preparation before return, and final exit, with alias macros binding generic names to the architecture implementations.

Floppy DMA operation selects between native and virtual paths based on capability flags, with virtual mode emulating transfers through programmed IO in the interrupt handler, tracking count residue address mode and active polling state, and falling back to virtual allocation when direct DMA memory is unavailable.
MSR access faulted inside machine check context never returns and spins on processor relax which issues a pause hint, while the BPF exception handler always declines handling by reporting false.

Fixed mapping page allocation panics when out of memory or misaligned, out of range fixed indices trigger a bug trap, thirty two bit walks bug when any intermediate level is missing, sixty four bit walks warn on table address mismatch, and callers rely on single entry kernel TLB flush after install.
